gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Lofree Flow 2 68 ($139.00 on its page) comes to $111.20 at checkout during Lofree's Black Friday Month, which is $18.75 below the NuPhy Air65 V3's $129.95; nor that Keychron's store lists the K7 Pro at $66.49, not the $73.49 ChatGPT showed.
standout_why: Compared against keebscout's low-profile guide, both mkbguide lists, keyboards.sh/size/65 and keyboardrecs. Keebscout prices the Flow 2 only as a 75% board at $199 and names the Air65 V3 without a price. Mkbguide's low-profile list says both families come in 68-key versions but gives no price or spec for them; its 65% list names none of the three. Keyboards.sh has only the K7 Max, at $90-$110. Keyboardrecs shows no prices. None gives a checkout price or puts the three 65% boards side by side at today's prices. The RTINGS pages (best list, both reviews, the compare page) returned only navigation to my fetches, so I could not check them. The score stays at 2, not 3, because I could not open NuPhy's product page to rule out a NuPhy cart discount, and the Lofree checkout figure is the desk's 11-21 cart read, not re-tested today.
decides: ChatGPT framed the Flow 2 68 as 'spend a little extra' over the Air65 V3 ($139.00 vs $129.95). At checkout through Lofree's sale the order flips: $111.20 vs $129.95, so the aluminum Lofree is the cheaper of the two near-ties until the sale ends (Nov 30 to Dec 1 per the desk rules). That supports featuring the Flow 2 68, which we can link through cj:lofree, as the pick or co-pick, with the Air65 V3 as the rival row at $129.95. The K7 Pro stays the budget row at $66.49, with no 2.4 GHz. No keyboard we already link is a 65% low-profile board (the Lofree records are 84-key; the Gamakay NS68 is 65% but not low-profile), so the page needs the Flow 2 68 added as a new record or it skips.

findings.value: None qualifies today: the Lofree records are all 84-key (75%), and the Gamakay NS68 is 68-key but a standard-height Hall effect board with 3.5 mm travel
